meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cook Islands (self-governing associated state within the Realm of New Zealand; incorporating jurisdiction of the International Company)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law with statutory offshore corporate code and customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No bilateral investment treaty is concluded directly in the name of the Cook Islands; the Cook Islands participates in PACER-Plus as a multilateral Pacific trade agreement, without investor-state dispute settlement.

A Cook Islands International Company is not automatically covered by New Zealand bilateral investment treaties or free trade agreements unless there is substantive economic activity in New Zealand; such coverage is generally unavailable for a tax-exempt international company.

No income tax treaty applies to a Cook Islands International Company because the entity is exempt from Cook Islands income tax and has no New Zealand taxable presence in the standard passive structure.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), as amended; Financial Supervisory Commission Act 2003; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2019 (Cook Islands); FSC AML/CFT Rules and Guidance; confidential beneficial ownership record-keeping obligations imposed on licensed international company service providers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss. 12-16 (incorporation), ss. 20-22 (company names), s. 96 (allotment of shares), s. 126 (board resolutions), s. 189 (registered office), s. 212 (directors' duties); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016; Income Tax Act 2007 ss. YB 3-4 (company residence and non-resident company classification)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered through the New Zealand Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 3: Application for Incorporation of a New Zealand Company (online), followed by issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and automatic allocation of a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be allotted for nil or nominal consideration; no escrow account, capital verification, or bank certification is required at incorporation; the company is classified as a non-resident exempt-zone vehicle for group internal purposes, with New Zealand-source taxation limited where central management and control is exercised outside New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (NEW ZEALAND LIMITED) — RESOLVED: (1) That the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby ratified and confirmed, and that the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number be accepted and retained in the Company's statutory records. (2) That the subscription for and allotment of ordinary shares in the capital of the Company be approved, and that the Register of Members be duly opened and maintained at the registered office. (3) That the registered office of the Company be established at the address listed in the application, and that the Registrar be notified of any change in accordance with s. 189 of the Companies Act 1993. (4) That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole Director of the Company, and [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary (if applicable), each to hold office until removed or replaced by further resolution. (5) That the Director be and is hereby authorized, either alone or jointly, to execute and deliver all documents, to open bank and merchant accounts (including Stripe Billing and Wise), to engage professional advisers, and to instruct the Companies Office and Inland Revenue as may be required to give full effect to these resolutions. (6) That the Company's constitution (in default form under Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993, or as separately adopted) be adopted and filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (online NZBN Companies Register name reservation module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the Companies Register to verify that the proposed corporate name is available and not prohibited under s. 20 of the Companies Act 1993. File an online name reservation application, supplying the proposed name, entity type, and intended activity, and pay the reservation fee by credit card. The reservation is a standalone application and does not yet incorporate the company.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of the proposed director
Proof of residential address of the proposed director
Proposed company name and concise statement of business purpose
Consent to act as director (online attestation or signed form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under s. 21 on the ground of similarity or offensiveness, file a written objection response with supporting trademark and business-name searches within 20 working days; alternatively, resubmit a revised alternative name for expedited reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (MBIE), online portal at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Form 3 online incorporation application. Enter the reserved company name, registered office address in New Zealand, principal place of business, director and shareholder particulars, share structure, and constitutional arrangements. Confirm adoption of the default constitution or upload a bespoke constitution. Submit the application electronically through the Companies Register and pay the statutory filing fee by credit or debit card.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate (reference number)
Default constitution (Schedule 2, Companies Act 1993) or bespoke constitution
Notice of registered office address in New Zealand
Consent to act as director duly signed
Shareholders' details and class-of-shares allocation
Certified identification documents (passport and utility bill) for all directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, query, or notice of refusal under s. 15, remedy the identified defects (e.g., incomplete consents, invalid office address, or name conflict) and resubmit the corrected data within 20 working days; if the application remains rejected, file a fresh application and request immediate reallocation of the reserved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (Companies Register electronic issuance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, download and retain the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the automatically assigned New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify that the registered company details (name, directors, shareholders, registered office) match the Filed application. Record the incorporation date and commencement of financial year in the company records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Companies Office
NZBN certificate
Registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate data is inaccurate, apply to the Registrar for correction under s. 214 of the Companies Act 1993; if the certificate is lost, request a certified copy from the Companies Office against payment of the official reissue fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (private corporate act, records maintained at the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting, adopt the pro forma first board resolutions, ratify the incorporation and share allotments, issue share certificates to the subscribers, open the register of members, appoint the director and any company secretary, and adopt the company constitution as the governing instrument. Ensure the statutory records are maintained in accordance with ss. 189-190 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of members and share register
Register of directors' and secretaries' particulars
Constitution (as adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: This step is internal; if any governance defect or inconsistency arises, cure it by a unanimous written resolution of the board or shareholders, and amend the statutory registers accordingly without requiring Companies Office intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD Number and GST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for an IRD number via the MyIR portal, supplying the NZBN and company details. Elect GST registration where taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per annum, or voluntarily if the business seeks input tax credits. Where the company is a non-resident exempt-zone entity with no New Zealand-source income, concurrently file the appropriate non-resident company declaration with Inland Revenue to manage any withholding tax and approved issuer levy obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Director and shareholder identification documents
Registered office address confirmation in New Zealand
Business activity declaration (ISIC 7410: specialized design activities)
Company constitution
Non-resident company declaration (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is held due to incomplete KYC or missing documentation, contact the Inland Revenue Business Services line (0800 377 774) and resubmit the corrected details through MyIR; the registration can be backdated to the incorporation date once verified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises, Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Local Authority (e.g., Auckland Council) and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For any physical office premises in New Zealand, obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) and confirm zoning/occupancy compliance under the Building Act 2004. Submit a fire evacuation scheme to FENZ where the workplace has more than 10 employees or is otherwise designated high-risk under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Implement all workplace health and safety documentation under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including hazard registers, worker engagement procedures, and electrical safety test certificates.
required_dossiers: Copy of the office lease agreement
Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) certificate from the local council
Fire evacuation scheme checklist (FENZ form)
Electrical test and tag certificates (AS/NZS 3760)
Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any building compliance notice issued under s. 125 of the Building Act 2004 by undertaking the required remedial works within the notice period; appeals may be lodged with the District Court. For FENZ objections to a fire evacuation scheme, revise and resubmit the scheme within 15 working days or apply to FENZ for a reasonable extension.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity of ISIC 7410 (product interface design and digital design subscription services) is not a licensed industry in New Zealand; no industrial manufacturing or sectoral licensing board has jurisdiction over this business scope. Where physical office premises are used, the territorial local authority (city or district council) administers building, zoning, and signage compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating license, manufacturing permit, or statutory industry authorization is mandated under New Zealand law for a digital design subscription agency operating solely on office-based infrastructure and remote delivery.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Schedule 1 of the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards) Regulations 2010; an office-based design and subscription service does not constitute a trade or industrial process requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment report, resource consent, or discharge permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The business generates no point-source wastewater or VOC emissions. General office waste and electronic waste must be managed in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and relevant council waste management bylaws. If the company introduces a backup diesel generator, printing/prototyping equipment, or any ventilation discharges, emissions must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ 2004) thresholds for PM10, PM2.5, and VOCs, and any trade waste discharge to sewer would require prior consent from the local water authority under the Local Government Act 2002.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) and annual fire systems compliance under the Building Act 2004; fire evacuation scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under s. 68 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 where the workplace accommodates more than 10 employees or is classified as high-risk. Occupational: full compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a hazard register, emergency response plan, worker training records, and AS/NZS 3760 electrical test-and-tag certification for all portable office equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake) – official portal: www.ird.govt.nz; business registration and GST filing via myIR secure online services and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry at www.business.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an International Company (CK_IC) treated as a non-resident foreign company, the statutory tax identifier is an IRD number. Procedure: (1) Obtain an NZBN from the New Zealand Companies Office if the entity is registered as an overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand; (2) Complete IR596 (Non-Resident Individual/Company Tax Registration) and file with Inland Revenue; or, for GST registration specifically, file IR830 (GST Registration) through myIR; (3) Provide certified supporting documentation (certificate of incorporation, director details, registered office, evidence of non-resident status) as required by Inland Revenue; (4) If the entity is incorporated in New Zealand but claims non-residence for tax, it must also lodge a declaration or obtain a residence determination under section YD2 of the Income Tax Act 2007.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident International Company with no New Zealand-sourced income; outside the New Zealand income tax net and not subject to entity-level NZ tax on foreign-source income; may still be liable for GST on remote supplies into New Zealand if the statutory threshold is exceeded).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not have a check-the-box regime. Entity classification is determined by domestic incorporation and central management-and-control rules under section YD2. An International Company may elect to be treated as a New Zealand tax resident if its central management and control is exercised in New Zealand, which would then bring worldwide income into the NZ tax net; alternatively, it may rely on the non-resident territorial tax regime. For GST, a non-resident supplier of remote services may elect to register under the simplified 'remote services' rules and apply zero-rating where the recipient is a GST-registered business (B2B). Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 restrict arbitrage, and no separate New Zealand 'look-through' election is available for international companies except for the standard Look-Through Company (LTC) rules that apply only to NZ-resident close-held companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – an offshore-supply VAT broadly aligned with the OECD International VAT/GST Guidelines
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 – a compulsory registration threshold applies to any person, including a non-resident international company, that makes taxable supplies in New Zealand in a 12-month period. For remote services (e.g., digital design subscriptions) supplied to New Zealand-resident consumers, the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies. If the International Company only supplies services to non-residents for consumption outside New Zealand, no GST registration is required unless the supplies connect with New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. GST returns are filed electronically via the myIR portal. E-invoicing is facilitated through the Pan-European Public Procurement On-Line (Peppol) framework, adopted mandatorily for New Zealand government departments since 2022, but private sector suppliers are encouraged rather than mandated to use it. There is no prior online approval of invoices; however, every GST-registered person must issue a valid tax invoice for taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) and retain sufficient digital evidence (contract, bank records, IP address, export documentation) to satisfy audit requirements. The Inland Revenue Department can require voluntary disclosure of electronic records under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies are eligible for zero-rated GST treatment under sections 11 or 11A of the GST Act 1985 if: (a) the supply is of goods that are exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply; or (b) the supply is of services to a person who is not resident in New Zealand and the services are not supplied for use/consumption in New Zealand (i.e., the services are performed remotely – such as UI/UX design subscriptions – and are not directly connected with New Zealand real property or movable property; or (c) the supply is of 'remote services' (electronically supplied services, such as subscription design platforms) to a non-resident business recipient that is GST-registered. The International Company must obtain and retain documentary evidence demonstrating the non-resident status of the recipient and the offshore consumption or exportation of the service, including the recipient's overseas billing address, foreign IP address, contract signed outside New Zealand, and evidence of payment from a foreign bank account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service – Trade Single Window) for physical goods; for services a detailed invoice or contract identifying supply type, value, and non-resident client
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (for physical exported goods) or equivalent electronic delivery logs evidencing offshore delivery of the subscription access
Inward Remittance Certificate (PDF) issued by a New Zealand bank certifying receipt of funds from abroad
Foreign exchange contract or SWIFT transfer records linking the payment to the non-resident client
Written supply agreement executed offshore showing that the UI/UX design services are consumed outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue scrutinises zero-rated export claims under section 11A and will claw back the input tax and assess GST at the standard 15% rate where the zero-rating is not substantiated within the required timeframe. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 include: a shortfall penalty of 20% (absence of reasonable care) or 50% (gross carelessness or abusive tax position) of the resulting GST shortfall; up to 100% for evasion or a fraudulent intent. In addition, use-of-money interest accrues from the original return due date. Where a GST refund has been claimed fraudulently, criminal prosecution can lead to fines of up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and NZ$250,000 for a company, plus imprisonment of up to five years. The International Company must retain zero-rating substantiation records for at least seven years and must comply with any Commissioner-issued record-keeping requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), operating jointly with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the New Zealand Exchange Control regime administered under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current account and capital account convertibility for the New Zealand dollar (NZD). There are no general restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, loan repayments, or dissolution proceeds for non-resident shareholders. The only meaningful hurdles are tax compliance obligations, including the requirement to maintain a New Zealand tax file number or to obtain an exemption from withholding tax if the payment qualifies under an applicable double tax agreement. Inbound capital injections and outbound operational disbursements may be effected freely, provided the underlying activity is not on a sanctions list and the instruction passes standard anti-money laundering and know-your-customer controls. Practical convertibility hurdles arise mainly at the commercial banking layer through correspondent bank due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owner and the declared business purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no mandatory surrender or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. Receivables may be retained offshore or converted into NZD at the discretion of the exporter. However, the New Zealand tax framework requires all foreign income of a New Zealand tax-resident entity to be declared on a worldwide basis, and transfer pricing rules require export transactions with associated enterprises to be conducted on an arm's-length basis. For the International Company structure, no statutory surrender framework is applicable, but bank account conduct rules require the underlying trade invoice and evidence of service delivery to support the clearing and crediting of export subscription revenues to the corporate operating account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for offshore digital EMIs, with heightened compliance friction. Legal constraints include the requirement under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's AML/CFT supervision framework that all account providers—whether domestic banks or registered financial institutions—conduct equivalent due diligence on non-resident companies. Purely offshore EMIs, such as digital banking platforms incorporated in other jurisdictions, may be permitted to open deposit accounts for the International Company only if they maintain a registered financial services provider (FSP) presence in New Zealand or rely on an inbound correspondence banking relationship. The preferred EMI route is through licensed New Zealand FSPs such as Wise New Zealand Limited or specialised fintech treasury platforms that offer segregated client money accounts and SWIFT-grade clearing rails. The practical constraint is that subscription revenue collected through Stripe Billing or Wise must ultimately settle into a New Zealand domestic bank account or an approved foreign currency settlement account to avoid the EMI being treated as a financial intermediary with additional reporting obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the International Company structure with non-resident ownership, the majority of New Zealand tier-1 banks permit fully remote onboarding through a video-verified KYC interview, provided that the ultimate beneficial owner, company directors, and operating signatories present certified passports, proof of residential address, and a corporate extract evidencing good standing. A physical branch appearance is mandatory only for in-person verification of original corporate documents if the company's registration jurisdiction is classified as high-risk or if enhanced due diligence determines that the directors cannot be adequately identified remotely. The recommended approach is to instruct directors and the beneficial owner to participate in a simultaneous video conference with a licensed New Zealand compliance officer, upload notarially certified corporate documents in the bank's secure portal, and execute the account mandate through an e-signature platform accepted by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company formed in a low-tax jurisdiction or with a tax-exempt classification trigger
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent certificate, certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, full register of directors and shareholders, tax classification ruling, and a written explanation of the genuine economic purpose for using the International Company for a UI/UX design subscription agency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and no local New Zealand director trigger
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports of all directors and beneficial owners, corporate ownership chart signed by the ultimate beneficial owner, professional legal opinion confirming the company's commercial purpose, and a full business plan for the design subscription agency showing invoicing and service delivery in New Zealand or from New Zealand as the regional commercial hub.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital subscription revenue model with high transaction velocity and cross-border payments trigger
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A copy of the SaaS / escrowed commercial agreement governing the UI/UX design subscription, active Stripe Billing configuration and settlement statements, WISE account statements, a reconciliation policy, sample customer invoices, and the company's internal AML/CFT policy for identifying the ultimate payment beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected deposits disproportionately high relative to stated tax-exempt structure trigger
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical financial statements or pro-forma cash-flow model, signed client master agreements, business bank reference from the company's incorporation service provider, and confirmation that the tax-exempt status applies only to foreign-sourced revenue and not New Zealand-sourced income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from the International Company's shareholder to its New Zealand operating account must be structured as a direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfer denominated in NZD or foreign currency, with the payment purpose coded as 'Equity Capital Subscription' or 'Shareholder Loan Contribution'. The relevant purpose code is not a static New Zealand customs code, but the instructing bank's transaction description should accurately state 'Capital Injection to NZ entity for design agency operations' to satisfy both NZ AML/CFT conduct rules and the New Zealand Companies Office reporting requirement in the annual return. Verification requires the provision of a shareholder resolution, a signed application for allotment or loan agreement, and the corporate certificate of incorporation in the bank's internal compliance system. Any inbound transfer above 10,000 NZD must be verified against the beneficial owner registry and the reasonable source-of-funds explanation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the UI/UX design subscription agency will be executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for fee, royalty, and intercompany cost-reimbursement payments, or through an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) if the transaction involves procurement of third-party design assets or software development services from a vendor that requires trade finance assurance. For subscription disbursements to overseas designers or licensors, the fastest clearing rail is preferential settlement through Wise or an NZ clearable SWIFT channel, with the payment description identifying the service nature. All outbound payments above 1,000 NZD trigger the bank's correspondent only if the receiving jurisdiction requires additional sanctions screening; otherwise, domestic NZ clearing plus the international wire system on the SWIFT network will be used. The company must retain in its treasury records an approved disbursement request, the underlying invoice, proof of delivery, and the signed contract to satisfy export-of-funds documentary requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright spot foreign exchange contracts for immediate conversion of USD subscription revenue to NZD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the NZD/USD pair for non-resident treasury desks requiring regulated forward pricing
Deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts executed with a registered New Zealand bank
Cross-currency interest rate swaps permitted for balance-sheet hedging, subject to the derivative activity being classified as treasury risk management rather than speculative dealing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Renewal Fee (International Company - Form IC-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (Realm of New Zealand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: must be filed and paid within one month following each annual incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the annual fee; continued default beyond 90 days may trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution from the International Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for the International Company under the tax-exempt regime; if converted to a New Zealand domestic company, an audit becomes mandatory only where total assets exceed NZD 60 million or annual revenue exceeds NZD 30 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) / New Zealand IFRS; financial statements are not publicly filed for the International Company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register; any shareholding transfers are recorded in the register of members and confirmed in the annual return, without public disclosure of UBO details.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,600 per year for registered agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (no statutory audit required); voluntary audit USD 3,000 - USD 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — statutorily exempt Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) under the International Companies Act; however, 28% is the New Zealand corporate headline rate if the same entity is found to be a New Zealand tax resident through central management and control in NZ.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption on all worldwide income derived by a compliant CK_IC; no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on share transfers, no estate duty; annual government fee and licensed agent fee are the sole recurring statutory costs. The 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' classification is achieved only while the IC does not carry on business from New Zealand, does not have a New Zealand fixed establishment, and maintains economic substance in Cook Islands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CK-IC Annual Return — filed in the Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA) online registry system through a licensed International Company service provider (registered agent). This is a registry annual return, not an income tax return; a tax-exempt IC makes no tax computation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the anniversary date of incorporation (or such shorter date imposed by the registered agent for processing before the FSDA deadline).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, date of incorporation, registered office in Rarotonga, and registered agent name/reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered office and agent address in Cook Islands; do not enter a New Zealand management or operational address because that would evidence NZ management and control.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential and service addresses, nationalities, date of birth, and contact details for each director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-residents of the Cook Islands, but at least one director must not be the sole shadow director and board meetings should not be effectively conducted in New Zealand; minutes should record Rarotonga as the venue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C - Shareholders and Beneficial Ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered shareholders, number/value of shares, and ultimate beneficial owner declarations under anti-money laundering rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; each beneficial owner must be identified to the FSDA. A nominee is permitted only if the nominee is a licensed international company services provider with a proper trust/control declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indication of any relevant activity under the Economic Substance (International Companies) Act, and confirmation of local substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a UI/UX design subscription business, state the actual core-income-generating activity and local connection; do not declare a New Zealand office because that may create a NZ permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a compounding late penalty, automatic default to FSDA warning notice, additional daily surcharge, suspension of the tax-exempt certificate, and ultimately strike-off/deregistration of the company; signatories and the registered agent may be separately fined.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return — New Zealand Inland Revenue (IRD) myIR electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: A New Zealand-resident CK_IC (or an IC with New Zealand source income) must file IR4 by the statutory due date; for a standard 31 March balance date the return is due by 7 July (paper) or the extended date if using an approved tax agent, with provisional tax instalments on set IRD dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income derived from the UI/UX design subscription service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the CK_IC has no NZ source income and is not NZ resident, this box is not required to be filed; if a NZ PE exists, include all NZ-source subscription revenue attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportioned operating expenses directly related to the design subscription business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses reasonably attributable to NZ-source business income are deductible; head-office/managed expenses must be apportioned on an OECD-compliant basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result after application of available deductions and imputation credits adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempt IC should show nil; a company that becomes NZ-resident cannot claim the Cook Islands tax exemption for the NZ taxable period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NRWT credits reversed to the income statement for distributions or actual payments to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC is treated as NZ-resident, submit certificate(s) of deduction to claim a credit against the final income tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under the Tax Administration Act 1994 plus late payment penalty accruing monthly on unpaid tax, use-of-money interest, disclosure of default under IRD debt collection, and director/company disqualification for persistent non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by a compliant Cook Islands International Company out of tax-exempt profits; Cook Islands imposes no dividend withholding or dividend distribution tax. If the CK_IC is nevertheless treated as a New Zealand tax-resident company, the domestic NRWT rate on non-resident dividends is 30%, with a 15% rate typically applied under several NZ double tax agreements for portfolio dividends and 0% for shareholder dividends where the treaty so provides.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No comprehensive double-tax agreement exists between the Cook Islands and New Zealand, and the CK_IC’s tax-exempt status would not support a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for Cook Islands treaty purposes. To claim any NZ DTA relief, the taxpayer must (i) be treated as a resident of the DTA partner country, (ii) hold a TRC from that partner’s revenue authority, (iii) be the beneficial owner of the income, (iv) execute the applicable IRD non-resident withholding tax declaration, and (v) maintain economic substance; a tax-exempt overseas IC that is not a resident of a treaty country should not claim treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Cook Islands: 0% withholding tax on royalty and interest paid by an exempt IC to non-residents. New Zealand: if NZ-resident status has arisen, the domestic NRWT statutory rates are 15% for both non-resident interest and non-resident royalties, unless reduced under a DTA (commonly 10% for royalties under some treaties) or replaced by the Approved Issuer Levy (2% on elective approved interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in an income year triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under s.78B of the Tax Administration Act 1994. A CbC report must be filed for multinational groups with consolidated annual group revenue of NZD 1.3 billion or more. In addition, the IRD may compel documentation for smaller transactions where a tax-exempt intermediate entity is interposed and there is no commercial rationale.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cook Islands Economic Substance (International Companies) requirements apply; an IC carrying on a relevant activity — which includes provision of services, headquarters, or IP-rich digital design activities — must demonstrate real economic presence in the Cook Islands through local offices, local qualified employees, board meetings directed and managed in the Cook Islands, and adequate operating expenditure. The ESR filing and any annual confirmation must be made through the FSDA, and information is automatically exchangeable with the New Zealand/Australian tax authorities under exchange-of-information arrangements. Failure to satisfy ESR means the tax exemption is withdrawn and significant penalties are imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Managing and Controlling the IC from New Zealand
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors and founders physically resident in New Zealand making strategic and operational decisions, executing contracts, marketing the UI/UX service, holding board meetings in Auckland, or maintaining the main bank account in New Zealand while claiming the IC is tax-exempt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IC is likely to be recharacterised as a New Zealand tax resident or as having a New Zealand permanent establishment; the Tax Exempt Zone status is void; IRD may assess all worldwide income at 28% with a shortfall penalty of up to 150% for evasion and criminal prosecution for the officers concerned.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax/penalties; the corporate veil may be pierced under s.135 of the Companies Act (reckless trading) and s.142 TAA; personal civil recovery, travel restrictions in relation to IRD debt, and imprisonment for criminal tax evasion are all available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a registered office service in Rarotonga and a licensed agent, with no employees, no in-island bank account, no local management function, and using the CK_IC purely as a tax-free invoicing shell for UI/UX subscription revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FSDA will impose economic substance penalties, withdraw the exemption, apply default interest and late fees, and may strike off the company; the company will be reported to the New Zealand IRD and to foreign tax authorities through automatic exchange of information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent may be personally fined for filing false ESR/beneficial ownership declarations; the directors can be disqualified and made personally liable for restitution to creditors if the stripping of assets leaves the company insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner; using nominee shareholders with undisclosed trust deeds; accepting subscription payments through Stripe Billing/Wise without transparent source-of-funds records and without filing suspicious activity reports in the Cook Islands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cook Islands AML/CFT Act and the Financial Intelligence Unit enforcement framework, the company and its MLRO are exposed to substantial monetary penalties, civil forfeiture, and imprisonment; the company can be added to the national AML risk register and its banking services terminated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Money Laundering Reporting Officer, directors, and beneficial owners face personal criminal liability, travel bans by FIU order, and seizure of funds; dishonest concealment of a true beneficial owner is treated as a predicate offence for money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Dressing up dividend free cash flow as 'management fees', 'software licences', 'loans', or 'design subcontract fees' from the CK_IC to a New Zealand shareholder/affiliate without documented contracts, board minutes, or arm's-length value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may recharacterise the payments under the general anti-avoidance rule (s.BG1 and s.GB21 of the Income Tax Act 2007), apply NRWT at 30% to dividends, assess the shareholder for personal tax, and impose evasion shortfall penalties plus use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve unlawful distributions or knowingly join in sham arrangements must restore the company’s funds (Companies Act 1993, s.60/financial assistance rules), and they can be made personally liable for amounts paid away; travel bans can be imposed to secure recovery.
